correctness.rationale: For one generator, two descents leave both products unchanged; exactly one descent forces unequal lengths. With no descents, equal products imply symmetric-group commutation, which preserves the adjacent pair as a set. Its swap would be a double descent, leaving only pointwise fixation. In the two-generator double-descent case with B the three consecutive labels and T its complement, fix the partial bijection T→T. If it leaves t rows and t columns unmatched in T, the unmatched T columns must appear among B rows in decreasing order, and their locations there are forced because every external label is less than all of B or greater than all of B. Inverse descents similarly force the unmatched T rows among B columns. Match the remaining B rows to the remaining B columns in reverse order. This is the unique double-descending completion, giving the sum of binomial squares times (m−t)! for t≤min(3,m). In either mixed case the two fixed positions and the two separately chosen outside matrix entries leave (n−4)! completions. The all-fixed case gives m!; in S_3 the mixed cases cannot occur, leaving identity and longest element. With a=i−1 the position term is a²+(m−a)², giving the stated size multiplicities and gap. The t=3 summand divided by n! tends to 1/36 with O(1/n) error, lower t contribute O(1/n), and the uniform mixed contribution is O(1/n²). In S_n the ordinary simultaneous centralizer fixes the triple pointwise and permutes its complement.
residual_risks: The reproduction is finite. The arbitrary-n conclusion follows from the order/completion argument. It is a count of monoid elements, not a dimension in the linear algebra.

value.rationale: Adjacent generators are the smallest interacting parabolic block, and their monoid centralizer tests the effect of the noninvertible length-increasing action under a natural commutation constraint. The exact four-stratum count isolates the source of genuine position dependence even though all these blocks have the same S_3 type and ordinary group centralizer size. It gives the full positional spectrum and a uniform comparison to the group case, not just one sample number.
residual_risks: No structural classification of the centralizer monoids or arbitrary generator subsets is asserted.
